title: Multiplying and Dividing in Scientific Notation

steps.body: To multiply in scientific notation: multiply the coefficients, ADD the exponents — the exact power-of-ten rule from Chapter 1. (3×10⁴) × (2×10³) = (3×2) × 10^(4+3) = 6 × 10⁷.
Build the exponent chain before multiplying the coefficients.

widget.prompt: For 10⁴ × 10³, step through the exponent chain and enter the exponent of the product.

numericErrors.feedback: Twelve multiplies the exponents. Multiplying equal bases combines all factors, so count 4 + 3 instead.
Keeping only the larger exponent loses the three additional factors of 10.

widget.successFeedback: The exponents add to 7, so 10⁴ × 10³ = 10⁷. Multiplying the coefficients then gives 6 × 10⁷.
widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the starting exponent and the addition stage before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Write out four factors of 10 followed by three more, then count all seven factors.

predict.prompt: When powers of 10 are multiplied, how do their exponents combine?
predict.reveal: Four factors of 10 followed by three more make seven factors in all. Therefore 10⁴ × 10³ = 10⁷, so the exponents add.

steps.body: Sometimes the coefficients multiply to 10 or more — then you must RENORMALIZE, shifting the extra factor of 10 into the exponent. (4×10⁵) × (3×10⁶) = 12 × 10¹¹, but 12 isn't between 1 and 10 — shift it: 12 × 10¹¹ = 1.2 × 10¹².

explanationVariants: Since 12 ≥ 10, shift one factor of 10 from the coefficient into the exponent: 1.2×10¹².

commonBuilds.feedback: That's the right VALUE, but not standard form — the coefficient must be under 10: 1.2×10¹².
Renormalizing 12 to 1.2 shifts the exponent UP by one too — it becomes 10¹², not 10¹¹.
That adds the coefficients instead of multiplying — 4×3=12, not 4+3=7.

widget.missFeedback: Multiply the fronts (4 × 3 = 12) and ADD the exponents — then renormalize 12 to 1.2.

options.label: 3 × 10⁷
options.feedback: That adds the exponents instead of subtracting — dividing means SUBTRACT: 5−2=3.

options.label: 4 × 10³
options.feedback: That subtracts the coefficients instead of dividing — 6÷2=3, not 6−2=4.

explanationVariants: 40 ≥ 10, so shift one factor of 10 into the exponent: 4×10¹¹.

commonBuilds.feedback: Renormalizing 40 to 4 shifts the exponent UP by one too — it becomes 10¹¹, not 10¹⁰.
That's the right VALUE, but not standard form — the coefficient must be under 10: 4×10¹¹.
That adds the coefficients instead of multiplying — 8×5=40, not 8+5=13.

widget.missFeedback: 8 × 5 = 40 renormalizes to 4, pushing the exponent up one: 10¹¹.

explanationVariants: 0.5 is below 1, so shift a factor of 10 the other way: multiply the coefficient by 10 and subtract 1 from the exponent.

commonBuilds.feedback: Renormalizing 0.5 up to 5 shifts the exponent DOWN by one too — it becomes 10⁻⁴, not 10⁻³.
That's the right VALUE, but not standard form — the coefficient must be at least 1: 5×10⁻⁴.
That divides backward (6÷3 instead of 3÷6) — 3÷6=0.5, not 2.

widget.missFeedback: Divide the fronts (3 ÷ 6 = 0.5) and SUBTRACT exponents — then renormalize 0.5 to 5.

explanationVariants: 42 ≥ 10, so shift one factor of 10 into the exponent: 4.2×10¹¹.

commonBuilds.feedback: Renormalizing 42 to 4.2 shifts the exponent UP by one too — it becomes 10¹¹, not 10¹⁰.
That's the right VALUE, but not standard form — the coefficient must be under 10: 4.2×10¹¹.
That adds the coefficients instead of multiplying (7+6=13→1.3×10¹²... check again: multiplying gives 7×6=42, not 13).

widget.missFeedback: 7 × 6 = 42 renormalizes to 4.2 with one more power of ten: 10¹¹.

steps.body: Multiply/divide coefficients and add/subtract exponents — then renormalize if needed.
takeaways: If the coefficient lands outside [1, 10), shift a factor of 10 into the exponent.
steps.teaser: Next: adding and subtracting in scientific notation — a different challenge entirely.

concept.body: Multiply coefficients and add exponents (or divide coefficients and subtract exponents); if the result's coefficient isn't between 1 and 10, renormalize by shifting a factor of 10 into the exponent.

explanationVariants: 2×4=8 and 3+2=5 gives 8×10⁵ — already standard form, no renormalizing needed.
8 is already between 1 and 10, so 8×10⁵ needs no adjustment.

options.label: 6 × 10⁵
options.feedback: That adds the coefficients instead of multiplying — 2×4=8, not 2+4=6.
